finalReport:
# OpenCut × OpenCode Integration — Technical Feasibility Today

**Verdict: Not stable today without a fork + browser-in-the-loop workaround.** The usable editor is the archived `opencut-classic` browser app with rich manual timeline editing but no stable programmatic surface; the main repo is an early rewrite preview where Editor API, MCP, headless, and plugin system are explicitly roadmap, not shipped.

**Budget disclosure:** Research closed in completion reserve with `researchRoundsRemaining=0`. Q1–Q3 are sufficient (6 SUPPORTED claims); Q4 automation/desktop is PARTIAL and licensing is UNSUPPORTED. This report marks what is verified fact vs roadmap vs workaround vs inference vs uncertainty and does not over-claim the uncommitted Q4/Q5 surface.

## 1. Verified facts (what is true in-tree today)

### 1.1 Two codebases — only one is usable now
**Verified fact:** `OpenCut-app/OpenCut` main states it **is being rewritten from the ground up** with coming items: Editor API, plugin-first architecture, Rust core for desktop/mobile/browser, MCP server for AI agents, headless mode, scripting tab. It directs users to `opencut-classic` as **the one to reach for today**, with production still on classic and rewrite as preview until takeover ([rewrite README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/main/README.md)).

**Implication for OpenCode:** Do not target main as a stable dependency. Pin any today-work to the archived classic lineage ([classic repo](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic)). Targeting main means tracking an unstable rewrite.

### 1.2 Editor and timeline model — strong manual, no programmatic path
**Verified fact:** Classic is a Next.js web app with multi-track timeline (video/audio/overlay), real-time preview, Zustand stores for editor/timeline/media/playback state, and browser video processing via FFmpeg.wasm ([architecture docs](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)).

**Verified fact:** v0.3.0 demonstrates manual-editing depth: masks, graph editor for keyframe curves, volume/speed controls, canvas backgrounds, stickers, multi-clip move/resize, independent X/Y animation, expandable keyframe lanes ([v0.3.0 release](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/releases/tag/v0.3.0)).

**Verified fact:** Contributor guidance makes timeline/project-management the focus but explicitly says **avoid preview and export** because they are being refactored to a new binary rendering approach; preview is DOM-based and inconsistent with export ([classic repo](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic)).

**Classification:** Manual timeline manipulation = verified fact. Stable external timeline mutation = does not exist (see §1.5).

### 1.3 Persistence — local-first browser storage, not files
**Verified fact:** Storage is `IndexedDB` for projects/metadata + `OPFS` for large media via a `StorageService` abstraction; later work scopes media and timeline per-project (`media-files-{projectId}`, timeline adapter per `projectId`) with auto-save on track updates ([storage refactor commit](https://github.com/realtgy/OpenCut/commit/bd0c7f22069d1a2e4b2a2d962becaf6b9e942414)).

**Verified fact:** Product docs confirm: IndexedDB for project data/metadata, local storage for preferences, all data stays on device, with automatic migration of old projects preserving original data ([project-management docs](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/features/project-management)).

**Implication:** There is no stable file-based `.opencut` project OpenCode can write from another process. Writes must go through the browser's IndexedDB/OPFS origin (same-origin Chromium profile) or a custom bridge you add.

### 1.4 Schema stability — high churn, known migration risk
**Verified fact:** Schema is actively versioned: v3→v6 migration for rich bookmarks/sticker IDs, plus v23→v24 and v25→v26 transformers in the rewrite; an open bug shows a failed migration caches a rejected promise, poisons retries, and can leave saving paused ([migration bug](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/871)).

**Classification:** Backward-compat guarantee = none verified (inference: assume breaking). Any direct IndexedDB writes or pinned `SerializedProject` compiler will rot without version pin + migration tests.

### 1.5 Automation surface — roadmap, not shipped
**Verified fact:** Editor API, MCP server, headless mode, scripting tab are listed as **What's coming** in the rewrite README, not as available APIs ([rewrite README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/main/README.md)).

**Verified fact:** Rewrite tracking lists headless (automation/batch/CI), MCP server, Editor/Plugin API, plugin host, project storage, scripting among unchecked tasks, and community analysis agrees the in-browser editor today **lacks a programmatic entry point** ([rewrite tracking](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811)).

**Classification:** No stable in-tree API/MCP/CLI/deep-link today = verified fact (absence evidenced by roadmap status). Third-party WS-bridge/MCP patches and Playwright controllers seen in search were **not committed as evidence** due to budget reserve → classified as **workaround/uncertainty**, not verified fact.

### 1.6 Rendering/export — interactive browser-only
**Verified fact:** Export reads tracks/media/activeProject, renders frame-by-frame to canvas, encodes via MediaBunny `CanvasSource` (avc/vp9), `Mp4/WebMOutputFormat`, `BufferTarget`, mixing audio via `AudioBufferSource` (aac/opus) with quality presets and progress/cancel ([export implementation](https://github.com/oldding/OpenCut/commit/70a9bfeeb196d5c0bde35ce0a165b696bb9ae1d0)).

**Verified fact:** Export requires WebCodecs; fallback drives canvas at real-time wall-clock via `captureStream` + MediaRecorder to WebM (60s timeline ≈60s, WebM-only), with optional server-side ffmpeg H.264 conversion; architecture remains local-first browser processing with only opt-in cloud features ([export fallback PR](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/pull/797)).

**Classification:** Local vs cloud = verified: local-first. Headless/batch = roadmap, not shipped ([rewrite tracking](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811)).

### 1.7 Process boundary and desktop — browser process, no stable desktop target
**Partial (weak):** No stable desktop build verified as a driver target; classic architecture is web/Zustand-centric and rewrite promises unified desktop/mobile/browser from one Rust-core codebase ([rewrite README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/main/README.md)) ([architecture docs](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)).

**Classification:** Inference, not verified fact: expect OpenCode (Node/CLI process) and OpenCut (Chromium origin with IndexedDB/OPFS + WebCodecs) to live in separate processes/profiles with no IPC. Any integration must bridge processes via localhost automation you own.

## 2. Fact vs inference vs roadmap vs workaround vs uncertainty

## 3. Feasible-today architecture (workaround — works but you own it)

Use only if you accept a fork and browser-in-the-loop:

1. **Pin `opencut-classic` fork** by commit hash. Do not float on main. Gate all upstream merges behind migration + export regression tests.
2. **Add an opt-in automation bridge in your fork only** (e.g., `NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTOMATION=1` injecting `window.__opencutAutomation`): `loadTemplate(DraftTemplate)`, `getTimeline()`, `exportProject({format,quality})`. Keep default builds untouched. This is a workaround, not upstream API.
3. **Keep OpenCode outside the browser:** OpenCode generates a versioned `DraftTemplate` JSON (your stable schema, zod-validated) + local asset manifest; a Node runner you own launches pinned Chromium via Playwright, loads your fork, injects assets via request interception or OPFS seeding in the same origin/profile, calls the bridge to compile `DraftTemplate→SerializedProject`, then triggers the existing in-browser canvas→MediaBunny export ([export](https://github.com/oldding/OpenCut/commit/70a9bfeeb196d5c0bde35ce0a165b696bb9ae1d0)) and pulls the buffer out.
4. **Persist outside the browser:** Treat IndexedDB/OPFS as cache only. Source of truth is `DraftTemplate` + assets on disk in OpenCode workspace. Rebuild browser state per render; never hand-edit browser storage.
5. **Constrain export expectations:** Require WebCodecs-capable Chromium; accept MP4/WebM via MediaBunny path, budget for real-time MediaRecorder fallback on incapable browsers ([fallback](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/pull/797)). No CLI/batch daemon — single warm Chromium profile is your render server.
6. **Pin schema + test migrations:** Snapshot `SerializedProject`/timeline types per fork commit; add automated load→migrate→export tests because churn and poisoning risk are verified ([migration bug](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/871)).

**Why this is not stable:** Every layer you rely on (timeline types, storage adapters, renderer) is flagged as refactoring/churning ([classic](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic)) ([migration bug](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/871)). Budget 20–40% ongoing maintenance for fork rebases.

## 4. Preferred future architecture (wait for rewrite to land)

Build on first-party pieces when they become SUPPORTED (none are today):

- **Rust core engine** separated from UI as single source of truth ([tracking](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811)).
- **Stable Editor API + Plugin API** for timeline/scene/media/project mutation with shared command/undo validation.
- **Headless runtime** reusing the same engine for batch/CI renders (replacing Playwright + 200MB Chromium workaround).
- **MCP server + scripting tab** as the OpenCode/agent surface instead of a custom bridge.
- **Versioned project storage** with documented migrations.

**Adoption gate:** Do not migrate until rewrite preview takes over production, Editor API is frozen/documented, and headless + MCP check boxes are closed in tracking ([tracking](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811)). Until then, treat local rewrite runs as research.

## 5. Blocking evidence (what would change the verdict)

1. Absence of automation is roadmap-status, not an oversight: Editor API/MCP/headless/scripting listed as coming ([rewrite README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/main/README.md)) and unchecked ([tracking](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811)).
2. No file-based integration point: persistence is origin-bound IndexedDB+OPFS ([storage commit](https://github.com/realtgy/OpenCut/commit/bd0c7f22069d1a2e4b2a2d962becaf6b9e942414)) ([docs](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/features/project-management)).
3. No compatible render daemon: export is interactive canvas→MediaBunny requiring a browser + WebCodecs ([export](https://github.com/oldding/OpenCut/commit/70a9bfeeb196d5c0bde35ce0a165b696bb9ae1d0)) ([fallback](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/pull/797)).
4. Stability risk is demonstrated, not hypothetical: version churn + poisoning bug ([migration bug](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/871)) plus explicit avoid-export/preview refactor notice ([classic](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic)).
5. Desktop/IPC gap is at best partial: no stable desktop target evidenced ([rewrite README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/main/README.md)) ([architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)).
6. Licensing remains a hard blocker to clear separately: UNSUPPORTED in this run — verify primary LICENSE and terms directly before embedding, forking, or commercializing; do not infer permissiveness from popularity.

*Remaining uncertainties carried forward: exact MCP tool surface, CLI shape, desktop packaging, license text, and third-party bridge quality — all require a follow-up run with completion budget, not assumptions.*

Scope: Feasibility of a stable OpenCode integration around OpenCut — editor/timeline, persistence/media, rendering/export, automation/process/desktop/MCP, compat and licensing.

Findings: Stable target today is archived `opencut-classic` (rich manual timeline, DOM preview under refactor) — main repo is an early rewrite preview. No stable in-tree Editor API, MCP, CLI, or headless exists; all are roadmap. Persistence is browser-local IndexedDB+OPFS (not files) with high schema churn and migration-failure risk. Export is interactive browser canvas→MediaBunny/WebCodecs only, no batch path. Feasible-today requires a pinned fork + custom bridge + Playwright-driven Chromium; preferred future is Rust-core + frozen Editor API + headless + MCP.

Uncertainty: desktop availability is PARTIAL, licensing is UNSUPPORTED (no committed evidence), automation Q4 incomplete — budget exhausted in completion reserve.

claimSummaries.statement: The stable editor today is opencut-classic (opencut.app); OpenCut-app/OpenCut main is an in-progress rewrite preview (new.opencut.app) and not a stable integration target.
Classic provides rich manual multi-track timeline editing (keyframes, masks, speed/volume) but preview/export are under binary-rendering refactor and inconsistent.
No stable in-tree Editor API, MCP server, CLI, or headless mode exists today; all are listed as coming/unchecked rewrite roadmap items.
Projects and media persist local-first in browser IndexedDB + OPFS, project-scoped with auto-save, not as stable files OpenCode can write directly.
Storage/project schema churn is high (v3-v6, v23-v26 migrations) with known migration-failure reliability risk.
